doesMyFigureMeasureTheSameThingAsTheCeil.answer: SAME POPULATION, SAME UNIT, DIFFERENT QUESTION -- so the ceiling is an upper bound on this figure, by construction.
doesMyFigureMeasureTheSameThingAsTheCeil.why: the A-199 ceilings are per-county counts of PARCELS whose absent-verified/refused cells the pin could remove (reconciled here per county as censusFalseAbsenceRemovedTotal: 5518/5116/18904/43305/103283/43346 -- the six numbers match the ceiling list exactly, in the same order). This lane's figure counts the subset of those parcels whose jurisdiction the pin actually makes ROUTABLE (a city that gains its first ruled table, or a district code the pin newly resolves). The gap (219,472 - 99,718 = 119,754 parcels) is the population whose jurisdiction still has no ruled table AT 1.4.0 -- unruled cities and unincorporated county area. So: check each apply against both numbers, and expect the observed value-cell writes to land between the pin figure and the ceiling on the districts the pin resolves, and to stay at 0 in jurisdictions with no table.
doesMyFigureMeasureTheSameThingAsTheCeil.cellsVsParcels: both figures are PARCELS. A parcel that moves gains 1..5 setback cells and 1..5 envelope cells (parcelAreaSqFt is written for every in-city parcel regardless), so per-cell counts are a multiple of these; this lane did not read the store and does not claim a cell count.

newlyFound: The Dockerfile installs from package.json alone (`COPY package.json ./` then `npm install --omit=dev`; no package-lock.json COPY). The lockfile therefore does NOT determine what the deployed writer resolves -- the exact pin string in package.json does. A caret pin would have been a silent drift channel into production while every local check stayed 1.4.0. Reported as a fleet lesson, not fixed here (the file is not this lane's to change... the pin SHAPE is, and it is exact).
